Nirmala Masi poured the tea and looked at Gurpreet, who hadn't touched her paratha.
'When I was twenty-five,' she said, 'I was a staff nurse in Ludhiana. I wrote to the matron that expired medicines were being relabelled and used. I did it properly, in writing. Nothing happened. Or rather, something happened to me.
Within a month I was on permanent night duty. My name disappeared from the training list. Someone started saying I was careless with records, that I was bitter because I'd been passed over. People I had shared tiffin with for three years stopped sitting near me in the canteen. Not because they hated me. Because they were scared.
That hurt more than the night shifts, beta. Being made into the problem.'
Gurpreet looked up. 'What did you do?'
'First,' Masi said, 'I stopped believing what they said about me.'

qa.q: What did Kamal and his brother fall out over?
qa.a: They fell out over their father's shop.

qa.q: Why did Kamal go silent after 'just forgive him and move on'?
qa.a: He likely felt dismissed, as if his hurt didn't matter, so he pulled away for two weeks.

qa.q: What changed when Arohi listened first and then asked a question?
qa.a: Listening fully and asking what Kamal wanted let him answer in his own words and start seeing his brother as a person.

qa.q: What does Kamal's answer 'I want him to know I was scared too' reveal about how he sees his brother now?
qa.a: It shows Kamal beginning to see his brother as someone who might also have been scared, a shift from pure bitterness toward understanding.

grounding: It shows a friend learning that 'just forgive' felt dismissive, while listening and asking what the person wants helped him see the other as human.
